tagline: The opinionated, compiled language for 2D games.

meta.title: Ludic — the opinionated game language
meta.description: Ludic is an opinionated, compiled language for 2D games. The entity system, rendering, named colors, input, deterministic math and save/load are part of the language — so you build a game, not a framework.
meta.og_description: An opinionated, compiled language for 2D games. The ECS, rendering, colors, input and save/load are built in — build a game, not a framework.

hero.lead: Ludic is an opinionated, compiled language for 2D games. The entity system, drawing, named colors, input, deterministic math and save/load aren't libraries you wire up — they're part of the language. You write the game; there's nothing to assemble first.
hero.pipeline_note: One step from your code to a native binary. No engine to install, no interpreter, no runtime to ship alongside it — the game is the executable.

features.title: A language shaped around the game.
features.intro: The things you normally bolt on — an entity-component system, a renderer, a deterministic clock, save/load — are primitives of the language itself. One opinionated way to do each, so there's little to decide and nothing to wire up.

cards.title: ECS in the syntax
cards.html: property, model, and handler are keywords. Query entities with query [A, B, {Tag}] and iterate matches directly — no framework to wire up.

cards.title: Deterministic runtime
cards.html: Q16.16 fixed-point math and a seeded RNG mean the same inputs produce the same frame — byte-for-byte — every run. Ideal for replays and lockstep netcode.

cards.title: Drawing & named colors
cards.html: The Screen API draws rectangles, text and pixels with named arguments; Color.Crimson and 220 more names read like English and cost nothing at runtime.

cards.title: One self-contained binary
cards.html: A game compiles to a single native executable — no engine to install, no interpreter, no runtime shipped beside it. Build, and run the file.

cards.title: Snapshot save/load
cards.html: save() and load() serialize the entire ECS world — every entity, property and program var — in one call.

cards.title: Scenes & state machines
cards.html: scene/layer/become model mutually-exclusive game states with enter/exit hooks; match/machine/state handle dispatch and per-entity FSMs.

cards.title: Retained UI & assets
cards.html: Declare a widget tree as data with ui — panels, labels, buttons, 9-slice skins, keyboard focus. Sprites decode from PNG at runtime; text is real TrueType.

cards.title: Modules & native calls
cards.html: module + @export fn builds a shared library of plain native symbols; extern fn … = "symbol" reaches out to any native library when you need the platform.

showcase.title: Real programs, one toolchain.
showcase.intro: The same ludicc that builds a JRPG builds a from-scratch Snake and a scene demo. Nothing is hardcoded to a genre — and every token below links into the reference.

samples.label: snake
samples.name: snake.ludic
samples.note: A complete Snake — grid, growth, food, game-over — from primitives. State is named vars, colors are named, and every draw call says what each argument is.

samples.label: scenes
samples.name: scenes.ludic
samples.note: One active scene at a time. `become` runs the old scene's on-exit and the new one's on-enter; layers draw in declaration order. State is a plain named var.

samples.label: lifecycle
samples.name: toggle.ludic
samples.note: Enable/disable at three scopes — entity, model, handler. Disabling never destroys data: a property's values persist, so a later enable restores them.

samples.label: hello
samples.name: hello.ludic
samples.note: The smallest program that exercises the whole pipeline: properties, a spawn, a queried handler, and a render/quit.

philosophy.title: No framework. No glue. Just the game.
paras: Most game code is plumbing — registering systems, wiring a renderer, threading state through a framework. Ludic makes those decisions for you and bakes them into the language, so the code you write is the game's actual logic.
Opinionated on purpose: one clear way to spawn an entity, draw a frame, name a color, run a scene. Less to choose, less to learn, less to maintain.

stats.lbl: clear way to do each thing

start.title: From clone to a native window.
start.intro: Build the toolchain once, then your game. Everything runs from the repo root.

steps.title: Build the toolchain
steps.html: bin/x build produces ludicc, the compiler you'll use for everything below.

steps.title: Compile & run an example
steps.html: bin/x app examples/games/snake.ludic turns a .ludic file into a native binary. Run it to open a real window.

steps.title: Go headless for tests
steps.html: --headless renders frames to a .ppm from piped input — deterministic output you can diff.

steps.title: Edit with full tooling
steps.html: bin/x tools builds the formatter and language server; every editor gets completion, diagnostics and go-to-definition.

terminal.comment: build and run an example (opens a window)

editors.title: One language server, every editor.
editors.intro: ludic-lsp speaks LSP 3.17 over stdio: context-aware completion, diagnostics from the compiler itself, go-to-definition and rename across imported files, and comment-preserving formatting. It even understands ```ludic fences in Markdown.
editors.note: bin/x tools builds ludic-fmt and ludic-lsp — the same formatter runs as a CLI for pre-commit hooks and CI.
